label: Stephen Bruehl
narrative: Bruehl is an unlikely but methodologically important entrant: a Vanderbilt professor of anesthesiology whose academic career is in pain research and statistical methodology, who has applied that statistical training to two of the field's better-controlled questions. In July 2025 he published a cluster analysis of features associated with UAP described in 216 selected reports from 1947 onwards through the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies, and on 20 October 2025 he and Beatriz Villarroel published in Scientific Reports the finding that transients in the Palomar Observatory Sky Survey may be associated with above-ground nuclear testing and with contemporaneous reports of unidentified anomalous phenomena. That is the single most consequential peer-reviewed result of 2025 for this board's central historical thesis, because it produces a statistical link, in a Nature-portfolio journal, between the atomic-weapons complex and anomalous optical transients over the United States in the years 1949-1957 - independent of any witness, any leak and any FOIA.
